title: Batnit
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites [Peah 8:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Peah.8.5) for Abba Shaul ben Batnit. Hyman says that his grandson was also called Batnit: [Nedarim 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.23a.3) relates that Batnit son of Abba Shaul ben Batnit found an opening for the vow of R’ Shimon son of Rabbi. Hyman says it SHOULD READ R’ Shimon, as at [the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim, chapter 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.9.1.6), because Batnit’s grandson could not have lived in the time of Shimon son of Rabbi. Or, he says, it SHOULD READ “of the descendants of Abba Shaul ben Batnit.”[^3]

notes.text: The compressed genealogy and chronology remain unresolved. Hyman offers two alternatives: changing Shimon son of Rabbi to Shimon, or reading a later descendant of Abba Shaul ben Batnit.
Hyman calls Batnit a grandson, then quotes a chain that names him as the son of Abba Shaul ben Batnit. Hyman’s two proposed readings are given in the translation.

The linked Mishnah names Abba Shaul. [The Bavli’s opening](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.22b.11) names the vower as R’ Shimon son of Rabbi, and the continuation gives Batnit son of Abba Shaul ben Batnit; [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=680&lang=en) cites the same episode. Yerushalmi Nedarim calls the vower R’ Shimon and gives the opening to a Galilean elder. The linked [Moed Katan parallel](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.3.1.14) calls the vower R’ Shimon son of Rabbi. Hyman proposes either a different name for the vower or a later descendant for Batnit.
